boxes.title: BEFORE WE BEGIN
boxes.body: Before we start turning things, a quick look at how a qubit's state is written down, and why we can picture it as an arrow on a ball.

boxes.title: A QUBIT'S STATE
boxes.body: A qubit's state |ψ⟩ is written as a column of two numbers, α ("alpha") and β ("beta"). α goes with the state |0⟩, and β goes with |1⟩. The bar and angle bracket around the 0, as in the label shown here, mark it as a quantum state.

boxes.title: COMPLEX NUMBERS
boxes.body: α and β are complex numbers. Each one has the form a + b<color=#FFE14D>i</color>, where a and b are ordinary numbers and <color=#FFE14D>i</color> is the number whose square is −1. So each complex number is really two ordinary numbers.

boxes.title: WHY COMPLEX?
boxes.body: Why not just ordinary numbers? Complex numbers carry an extra ingredient called phase. Phase is what lets quantum states interfere with each other. You will see it in action later in this lesson.

boxes.title: FOUR NUMBERS
boxes.body: Two complex numbers make four ordinary numbers. Two ordinary numbers can be drawn as an arrow on a flat page. Four cannot be drawn on a page, or even in the room around you.

boxes.title: TWO ARE NOT FREE
boxes.body: But two of the four are not free. First, the sizes must add up to one: <nobr>|α|² + |β|² = 1</nobr>. Second, shifting both numbers by the same phase changes nothing you could ever measure, so it is ignored.

boxes.title: THE BLOCH SPHERE
boxes.body: That leaves two numbers: two angles. Two angles pick out a point on a sphere, the way latitude and longitude pick out a place on a globe. This sphere is called the Bloch sphere. |0⟩ is at the top and |1⟩ is at the bottom.

boxes.title: HEIGHT AND DIRECTION
boxes.body: Keep the globe in mind. The height of the arrow, like latitude, will decide what a measurement gives. The direction around the middle, like longitude, is the phase.

boxes.title: GATES ARE TURNS
boxes.body: Any change to a qubit, short of measuring it, is a 2 × 2 matrix called a unitary. On the sphere, every unitary is simply a turn of the arrow. The rest of this lesson is about these turns.
